rationale: ROUND 2 of trail 3626629a. REVISE was right on every gating count, and two of the objections changed the CODE, not just the prose. GATING (prior_art_librarian, HIGH): migration 551 UPDATEs by type='section-editor' while a landmine documents four agent types carrying TWO active rows, of which only the higher version loads — so an UPDATE-by-type can silently arm the row nobody reads. NOT CHECKED BEFORE BEING ASSERTED SAFE, and the seat is right that it was asserted. CHECKED NOW: section-editor has exactly ONE live row (id 2ed3b581, version 1), and the four duplicated types are chief-strategist, content-creator, content-creator-contact and site-component-architect — section-editor is not among them. The migration's existing precondition is the right guard and its message now NAMES the four, so a future duplication aborts with the reason rather than a bare count. prior_art medium 2 — 'exactly one consumer of apply_section_edit' was a load-bearing ABSENCE claim with no attached query. Attached: top-level scan returns exactly one row (section-editor.apply_edit) and the one-sub_workflow-level scan returns zero. prior_art medium 3 — '0 armed today' was quoted from a prior measurement. Re-measured THIS ROUND: record key 0 rows, refuse key 0 rows. bug_historian medium — THE OBJECTION THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN, and it is this bug's own shape used against my plan: arming DETECTION on chrome while only the section editor got PROTECTION is 016b §9's 'one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix, the sibling stays heuristic', and the 0-rows measurement is a population snapshot, not a structural guarantee. The chrome store path now has the SAME refusal, through the SAME decision function (refusePersistForAbsentRequired) — default OFF and, deliberately, NO migration arms it: with zero rows able to trigger it, arming would arm an unexercisable refusal, while omitting the capability would mean the first chrome component adopted with a required field needs a code change, a review and a roll before it can be protected. This way it needs a config flip, and the trigger to flip is named: the first required_fields_missing item with surface='site_component'. Its disposition mirrors the execution-failure branch three lines above it rather than inventing a second one — decline to store, previous bytes keep serving, and escalate as fatal ONLY where the slot has nothing stored at all, because a site must not go live with a missing header. A new test asserts the two persist paths share ONE decision on all four arming×finding combinations, so a forked chrome implementation fails. guidelines medium — 550's post-verify walked only the top level, i.e. it certified exactly the coverage the write can reach and called it full. The post-verify now ALSO walks config.sub_workflow.steps and RAISEs on any unarmed nested occurrence, so a nested step added between the pre-check and the COMMIT cannot pass as covered. Re-measured this round: top-level 7, nested 0. guardian medium — the seven steps are now ENUMERATED BY OWNING AGENT TYPE in 550's header (nav-link-fixer, nav-updater, pageflow-builder, rerender-chrome, rerender-pages, rerender-site, site-work-orchestrator), with the note that none is a duplicate-active-row type and that the loop writes BY ROW ID so a duplicate would be armed consistently rather than half-armed. Its two low objections are taken: both migration edits are relabelled config_change. bug_historian low — 551's canary now checks THREE things, not one: the live section byte-identical (md5 before/after), the required_fields_missing item present (refusing must never be why a defect goes unrecorded), and the DRIVING item's terminal status READ rather than assumed benign — expected to read complete until bugs_open/344 lands, with 344's own fingerprint (retry_after > completed_at on a complete row) named so the reader knows what they are looking at. editquality low — render_seam_absent_required_test.go is PRE-EXISTING (created by trail bb7f5d0e, six tests) and this round appends to it; the operation stays modify and the plan now says so. architecture low — the optional-key budget is reported: apply_section_edit declares 7 optional INPUTS and this is a CONFIG key, which cmd/config-key-audit --optional-key-budget does not count, so the action stays at 7 of 10 and no accumulated-surface review is owed. UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1: the defect and the placement. The two section-editor routes write rendered_html straight onto an already-live page with no validate_content between, and today they file the required_fields_missing item and then persist the blank anyway — detection without protection on the highest-exposure path. The gate sits at the ONE persist switch, the same placement rule as the link repair (136) and the envelope refusal (190) in the same function, so a future edit branch inherits it. Opt-in, default OFF (owner 2026-08-02 §2); RFC_022's three conditions hold with queries attached, not asserted. Mutation-proven: inverting the deciding arm fails two tests, reverting greens them. Honest limit still stated: the in-branch copy onto sectionEditOutcome needs a database, so it is covered by the post-roll canary, not by a unit test.

plan.risks: RISK 1: The refusal fails a step with no error_step, so until bugs_open/344 lands the DRIVING work item of a refused edit may be stamped complete by the dispatch loop. Mitigation is inherent rather than procedural — the live page is untouched because the write never happens, and the required_fields_missing item is filed BEFORE the refusal on every path (editor and chrome alike), so the defect is on the queue regardless of the driving item's status. 551's canary now READS that status rather than assuming it benign. 344 owns the completion fix; this round does not touch it. RISK 2: The armed editor refusal changes edit outcomes — an edit that today persists a blank required field will fail once 551 applies. That is the intended authority change, it is opt-in, and 551 is the visible act on the one live consumer after the roll. The seam judges the MERGED map (fleet defaults included), so it fires only where the field would genuinely render empty: a strict subset of the writer-side gate's population, pinned by TestSeamReportsASubsetOfThePreRenderGateAndSaysWhy. RISK 3: The chrome refusal ships UNARMED and could therefore rot unexercised — the estate's stated cost of default-OFF switches. Accepted deliberately and with a named trigger (the first required_fields_missing item with surface='site_component'), because the alternative shapes are worse: arming an unexercisable refusal today, or leaving the first adopting site to wait for a code change, a review and a roll. The shared-decision test is what keeps the unarmed path honest — it cannot silently diverge from the armed one. RISK 4: Arming the chrome RECORD could flood the queue if the population were misjudged. Measured 0 rows fire today (re-verified this round), and the emitter co-dedups with the post-deploy check on the shared item_key shape, so even future firings converge on one item per page/slot. RISK 5: 550's write reaches only top-level steps. The pre-condition refuses on a nested occurrence AND the post-verify now walks the nested structure too, so the failure mode is an abort, never a false certificate. RISK 6: The unit tests cannot see a branch that stops copying AbsentRequiredFields onto the outcome (it needs a database). Stated in the test's own comment and covered by 551's post-roll canary — one refusing edit and one clean edit in the same run.
